findings.reason: Proof 3.1 claims the conditional qubit after measuring k, but the listed projective-measurement prerequisites establish outcome probabilities only. State the Lüders instrument/update rule and derive the conditional state. Affected consumers: alg-qa-dihedral-hidden-subgroup-sieve Step 1 and thm-qa-dihedral-sieve-scope F2, Steps 2.1 and 3.1.

Statement and Proof 2.1–3.1 claim post-measurement qubit states, while the listed PVM prerequisites do not specify a state update. Explicitly use the Lüders instrument and its conditional-state rule. Affected consumers: alg-qa-dihedral-hidden-subgroup-sieve Step 2 and thm-qa-dihedral-sieve-scope F3, Steps 2.1–2.2.

Step 4 says to restrict the oracle to K0/K1 but does not specify how child coordinates are queried through the ambient oracle. Under the stated convention the inclusions are (a',b')→(2a',b') and (a',b')→(2a'+b',b') modulo 2^r. State the maps and account for their per-query cost.

Proof 1.2 extends its bound on the b_i sum through t_r=m, where it is not established: for m=t_r=3 the recurrence gives C_3=52677/32768≈1.608, not >2 as claimed. Prove a sufficient bound such as C_t>1 for Step 3.1, or adjust the absence estimate. Also state whether O(n^3 M) excludes F-oracle implementation gates; the f,g-to-F wrapper adds O(w_F) ordinary gates per call, and Step 6.1 already leaves an explicit-oracle gate term separate.

The claim that both sources refer elsewhere for associativity is inaccurate. Childs §7.1 says an explicit check (e.g. with Mathematica) can establish it; Proos–Zalka §3 points to reference [14]. Neither passage supplies a detailed local proof. Correct the source description while retaining the scope limit. [Childs, Lecture Notes, §7.1](https://www.cs.umd.edu/~amchilds/qa/qa.pdf); [Proos–Zalka, §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0301141).
